result.topic_en: Pencil calculations of a fourth-order partial differential equation in the variables log r and φ with trigonometric coefficients, equated to μ^4 u; a triangular scheme of series coefficients a_{m,n}; a recursion factor 4(m+1)(2m+1); and a fragment involving cos and sin of √(1−β)a.
result.transcription:
$\left(\frac{\partial^4 u}{(\partial\log r)^4}+2\frac{\partial^4 u}{\partial\log r^2\,\partial\varphi^2}+\frac{\partial^4 u}{\partial\varphi^4}\right)\left[r^2+\frac{1}{r^2}+2+4\cos(\varphi-\psi)\cos(\varphi+\psi)-2\left(r+\frac1r\right)\left(\cos(\varphi-\psi)+\cos(\varphi+\psi)\right)\right]$
$\left(\frac{\partial^3 u}{(\partial\log r)^3}+\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial\log r\,\partial\varphi^2}\right)\left(r^2-\frac{1}{r^2}\right)-2\left(r-\frac1r\right)\left(\cos(\varphi-\psi)+\cos(\varphi+\psi)\right)$ $\quad -4\cos\varphi\cos\psi$
$\left(\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial\log r^2\,\partial\varphi}+\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial\varphi^3}\right)\left(-4\sin 2\varphi+2\left(r+\frac1r\right)\left(\sin(\varphi-\psi)+\sin(\varphi+\psi)\right)\right)$ $\quad 4\sin\varphi\cos\psi$
$\left(\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\log r^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\varphi^2}\right)\left(r^2+\frac{1}{r^2}-2\cos 2\varphi\right)=\mu^4 u$

methods.what: Fourth-order PDE in polar-logarithmic coordinates with trigonometric coefficients, an eigenvalue problem with eigenvalue μ^4
Triangular scheme of double-indexed series coefficients for a recursive solution
Recursion: the coefficient (m+2,m) is obtained from (m,m) by dividing μ^4 times it by 4(m+1)(2m+1)
Algebraic simplification of the recursion denominator
